claims.text: Boris describes AI-authored code plus human review.
Simon says he often tries three design prototypes and advocates real-user usability testing to help assess options.
claims.notes: 22:11–23:35 re-read from acquired automatic captions. Actual prototyping practice distinguished from proposed usability testing.

claims.text: Kent points to business obligations beyond a visible feature.
claims.notes: 2:14:13–2:15:39; no compliance guidance or savings claims used.

claims.text: Microsoft Digital reports moving intent and acceptance into specifications.
claims.notes: Organizational self-report, not neutral performance evidence.

claims.text: Ritchie describes expression and comprehension advantages above assembler.
Lower implementation cost makes problem selection and demand discovery more salient.
claims.notes: Aaron interpretation; AI also assists upstream; not an employment forecast.

claims.text: Aaron has described a Dev Linux/Windows report round trip.
claims.notes: Approved source: src/content/blogs/2026-09-06-astra/gpt-6-astra-real-work-zh.md, section 1. No claim of production readiness or measured speedup.

claims.text: Microsoft Digital reports that faster individual development did not initially translate to team productivity, prompting process changes.
claims.notes: Rechecked 2026-09-07, article opening. Organization self-report, not an independently measured general result.

claims.text: In September 2024 Amazon described excessive layers and processes and announced organizational flattening.
claims.notes: Body paragraphs on manager layers and process. Does not establish surplus headcount percentage or imply AI did not yet exist.

claims.text: In June 2025 Andy Jassy expected extensive AI use to reduce total corporate workforce over the following years, with fewer people in some types of work and more in others.
claims.notes: Expectation stated by management, not measured realized reductions attributable to AI.

claims.text: The January 2026 reduction announcement again stated reducing layers, increasing ownership and removing bureaucracy as organizational goals.
claims.notes: No claim that these statements exhaust causes or assess the contribution of affected individuals. Draft does not use the 16000 count.

claims.text: Aaron describes a considered judgment from his earlier Amazon employment: organizational staffing and expansion did not necessarily track customer value. He says later restructuring and layoffs did not surprise him.
claims.notes: Current author clarification recorded in revisions/full-redraft-03/feedback.md. Subjective judgment, not independently verified. No discomfort, numerical workforce estimate, team details, or all-layoff causation asserted.

claims.text: Aaron interprets lower execution costs as a catalyst for re-examining existing organizational structures and staffing.
claims.notes: Author interpretation consistent with stated plans, not proof of causes of all layoffs or lack of value of affected people.
